method: SFCW ground-based radar: apply iFFT to the stepped-frequency return to form range bins; estimate consecutive-pulse phase difference and convert it to displacement; assess temporal coherence; use a 3-bin boxcar and an empirical triangular-wave matched filter/convolution to suppress noise and trigger genuine bridge-vibration peaks.
evidence: Author manuscript reports a 5–6 GHz SFCW radar with 15 cm slant-range resolution and 33 Hz PRF. The method uses iFFT range compression, consecutive-pulse phase difference for motion, a 5-bin temporal-coherence check, 3-bin boxcar smoothing, and an empirical matched filter in the frequency domain. Truck-induced bridge oscillations of about 1 mm were observed; the largest detected peaks were about 0.3 mm.
evidence_locator: author manuscript pp. 1–4, Table 1, Sections 2.1–2.2, 3.2–4; local text R1691.txt
transfer_limit: SFCW/33 Hz bridge experiment is a precursor for range-bin phase and peak detection, but its PRF and low-frequency setup do not establish IWR performance below 100 Hz or 10 micrometres.

method: Sentinel-1 MT-DInSAR bridge anomaly pipeline: group non-uniform measurement points into zones, average LOS displacement, combine ascending/descending tracks to estimate East/Up components, fit a temperature-to-longitudinal-displacement linear regression by least squares, and use residuals with a Hotelling T² control chart for anomaly detection.
evidence: Official proceedings PDF states that Sentinel-1/EGMS InSAR amplitude and phase yield LOS displacement; zone averages are combined from ascending and descending tracks; a temperature regression predicts reference displacement; residuals feed a T² control chart with a 5% upper control limit. The case study identifies anomalous trends before the Longobucco Bridge collapse.
evidence_locator: official proceedings PDF pp. 2–7, Sections 2–3 and Conclusions; local PDF and extracted text R1727.txt
transfer_limit: This is satellite MT-DInSAR and long-term anomaly detection, not high-rate IWR vibrometry. Transferable parts are LOS geometry, temperature compensation, residual quality statistics and control-chart gating.
